- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often overcorrects downward — adjust upward to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- Model frequently overestimates short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% above recent mean) — cap forecast growth after 2–3 consecutive days of high sentiment.  
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — if 10+ consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should be slightly above recent low to reflect resilience.  
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model lags — forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.  
- Model consistently underpredicts true outcomes in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is 0.33–0.67.  
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +10%+ above prior peak) — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model tends to overforecast — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
